authority.citation: Baethge C, Goldbeck-Wood S, Mertens S. SANRA—a scale for the quality assessment of narrative review articles. Research Integrity and Peer Review. 2019;4:5.
authority.adaptation: Concise paraphrased execution rules; not an official instrument revision. Verify against both original figures before an appraisal epoch.

limitations: Evaluate all six items against the whole manuscript, including its abstract.
The instrument does not certify factual correctness, content completeness, originality or clinical applicability.
Do not translate its sum into a universal low/high risk-of-bias or GRADE category.
NO_INFORMATION indicates incomplete appraisal evidence; it is not an official SANRA score and must not be summed as zero.
Report six item judgments with reasons. Sum only six resolved scores; do not invent cross-setting quality thresholds.

domains.question: How explicitly is importance justified for the intended readership?
domains.rule: 0: no justification. 1: importance only alluded to. 2: explicit justification. Assess the journal/readership context and identified problem or evidence gap.

domains.question: Are concrete aims or questions stated?
domains.rule: 0: none. 1: general or unclear aims. 2: at least one concrete aim or question. Do not infer an explicit aim merely from the title.

domains.question: How transparently is the literature search described?
domains.rule: 0: search methods unmentioned. 1: brief description. 2: detailed description including search terms and included literature types/criteria. Systematic-review-level search documentation is not required.

domains.question: Do references support the key statements?
domains.rule: 0: key statements supported sparsely or not at all. 1: inconsistent support. 2: all or almost all relevant key statements supported. Uncontroversial statements may reasonably need no reference.

domains.question: Is appropriate evidence used in the argument?
domains.rule: 0: hardly any appropriate argument/evidence. 1: evidence introduced selectively or superficially. 2: appropriate evidence generally present, including study designs and available evidence levels. Separate this from numerical presentation.

domains.question: Are relevant outcome data appropriately presented?
domains.rule: 0: inadequate presentation. 1: partially appropriate presentation. 2: generally appropriate relevant outcomes and uncertainty. Judge relevance for the field, including absolute/relative effects and clinical/surrogate endpoints where applicable.
